verdict.reasoning: Printed page 915 (folio 891, Annex E item 18) shows an unruled, borderless two-column list: header 'New exception-names' / 'Exception-names in the previous COBOL standard', then three rows EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND/EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND, EC-FUNCTION-ARG-OMITTED/EC-PROGRAM-ARG-OMITTED, EC-OO-ARG-OMITTED/EC-PROGRAM-ARG-OMITTED. The markdown has every word, all six names, in the same order with the same row pairing, one row per line. Each exception-name is a single hyphenated token, so a row of two tokens cannot be split any other way, and the old-to-new correspondence is not lost. The only thing lost is the whitespace column alignment, which is layout. The header row is prose labels in an informative annex. No content or meaning differs.
